content.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   windows     build-windows.yml windows-x64 app zip (fa-app-windows-x64.zip,
#                                 stable name), attached to the next-tag
#                                 release — the Windows counterpart of the
#                                 TestFlight leg: one release-quality GUI
#                                 app build per day (gh-2140)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - windows
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - windows
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, wait for it read-only, fail on any non-success conclusion.
  # The child run URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt
  # its log.
  #
  # ── The gh-1903 invariant: queued on the single self-hosted runner is
  # HEALTHY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # dispatch_and_watch.sh NEVER cancels or re-dispatches a child mid-watch.
  # A child queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is normal
  # operation; the old #344 budget + gh-172 queue-stall watchdog cancelled
  # two such healthy queued children on 2026-10-26 (daily run 40274465122,
  # tracking issue #1735 — those cancellations were THIS defect, not an
  # ASC/IPA problem) and failed a fully-built v1.0.648 solely by killing
  # its place in line. What bounds a slow child instead:
  #   * every job in a watched child chain carries an explicit
  #     timeout-minutes — a wedged self-hosted job self-fails server-side
  #     (#344; a job-level timeout is enforced BY the runner, which is why
  #     a hung worker outliving its own ceiling is the one class the
  #     server cannot kill), and
  #   * the leg timeout-minutes below — when it fires, the runner TERMs
  #     the watcher, which cancels ONLY this leg's own NEVER-STARTED child
  #     (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) so an orphaned queued run cannot publish
  #     unattended, then fails naming the child run, its last observed
  #     state, and the observed pool activity (gh-172 diagnostic).
  # While the child has not started, the watcher logs sibling in-progress
  # runs on a diagnostic interval — read-only; cannot-observe ⇒
  # cannot-judge ⇒ never a cancel.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351, leg-timeout sizing) ────────────────────────
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Invariant: leg timeout > child worst-case +
  # margin (appear window 60×10s ≈ 10m + poll slack ≈ 5m) — the leg always
  # outlives a healthy slow child, which is now NEVER killed.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  ;  360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   ;  240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  ;  360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases grew by exactly the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   ;  180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   ;  150m
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20) history: the re-dispatched
  # testflight child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker —
  # the leg burned its remaining ~107m and died as a bare 360m ceiling
  # kill with no diagnosis. The budget/stall watchdog built to catch that
  # faster could not tell a zombie-held pool from a sibling leg's job
  # legitimately occupying the shared fa-m5-1 (its own comment admitted
  # it), and its 31m stall window did not cover the cli sibling chain's
  # 335m worst-case — so it false-cancelled healthy queues by design
  # (gh-1903, #1735). The zombie goal is now met by the bounds above plus
  # the leg-timeout orphan-cancel diagnostic, not by a heuristic that
  # cannot tell a queue from a zombie.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120); 360m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. The 360m cap
    # also bounds any gh-172 zombie wait — on leg timeout the watcher's
    # orphan-cancel kills only this leg's never-started child (gh-1903).
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903, correlation from #343): correlates
          # OUR run by the child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" —
          # displayTitle is the only distinguisher in the run-list API),
          # newest match in a tight window. Waits READ-ONLY: a child
          # queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is healthy and is
          # never cancelled/re-dispatched; the bounds are build-ios/
          # submit-ios's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 360m.
          # On leg timeout the watcher cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child (gh-1903) — see the leg-header
          # comment for the full invariant.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30);
    # 240m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. Waits are read-only (gh-1903) —
    # no cancel, no re-dispatch, bounded by the child's per-job timeouts
    # (#344) and this leg timeout.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window. Read-only wait (gh-1903): a wedged/queued run
          # is NEVER cancelled or re-dispatched — build-android/submit-
          # android's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 240m are
          # the only bounds; on leg timeout only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child is cancelled.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15); 360m leg ≥ worst-case + margin
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344). A
    # queued child — including one waiting out a sibling's full 150m
    # matrix leg — is NEVER cancelled (gh-1903); the leg timeout bounds
    # the wait and the watcher orphan-cancels only a never-started child.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343):
          # correlates OUR run by the child's run-name
          # ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a concurrent human
          # dispatch is never adopted. A wedged self-hosted run is NEVER
          # cancelled/re-dispatched — the bounds are the build-macos jobs'
          # own 150m server-side timeouts (#344) and this leg's 360m; on
          # leg timeout the watcher orphan-cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started child.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  windows:
    name: 'Leg: Windows app'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 85m (version 20 + windows build 45 +
    # attach 20); 150m leg > worst-case + margin (the addin-leg sizing).
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'windows')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'windows'
        run: |
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-windows.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The child derives the version itself (same latest-tag+1 math as
          # build-macos/build-mobile — all release children derive the SAME
          # next tag). Shared watcher (gh-1903): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name, waits READ-ONLY within the child's own
          # timeout bounds, orphan-cancels only this leg's never-started
          # child on leg timeout.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-windows.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-windows (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15); 180m leg
    # ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could not
    # even fit a healthy child + appear window — the 180m leg is the
    # #351 sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # pages.yml takes no inputs, so there is no displayTitle to
          # disambiguate on — the watcher falls back to
          # newest-in-tight-window and waits read-only: no cancel, no
          # re-dispatch, bounded by the pages jobs' own timeout-minutes
          # (#344) and this leg's 180m.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job); 150m
    # leg ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could
    # not even fit a healthy child + appear window — 150m is the #351
    # sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node +
      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # No inputs to disambiguate on (newest-in-tight-window
          # fallback); the wait is bounded by the office-addin-suite
          # job's own 45m timeout (#344) and this leg's 150m — never by a
          # watcher cancel.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint

          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}

name: Build macOS Release (Fa)

          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps

      - name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework

          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0

          set -euo pipefail

          # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
          #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
          #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
          #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
          #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
          #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
          #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
          #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
          #
          #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
          #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
          #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
          #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
          #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
          #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
          #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
          #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
          #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
          #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
          #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
          #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
          #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
          #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
          #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
          # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
          # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
          # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
          # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
          ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
          # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
          # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
          # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache. The pinned byte size tells a
          # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
          # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
          ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
          ASSET_BYTES=97238501
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # fa-m5 host warm cache (owner-provisioned): persistent
            # CI-authentic zips in ~/vendor-cache/ (per-arch names matching
            # $ZIP's basename), launchd-refreshed. Cold-/tmp fallback: seed
            # from a digest-verified CANDIDATE — the gh-1759 invariants
            # stay literal: the partial itself is never removed before the
            # loop (gh-1759), and a bad candidate is discarded by its own
            # name without touching the partial.
            SEED="$HOME/vendor-cache/$(basename "$ZIP")"
            if [ ! -f "$ZIP" ] && [ -f "$SEED" ]; then
              SEED_CANDIDATE="$ZIP.host-seed"
              cp "$SEED" "$SEED_CANDIDATE" 2>/dev/null || true
              if echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $SEED_CANDIDATE" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                mv "$SEED_CANDIDATE" "$ZIP"
              else
                rm -f "$SEED_CANDIDATE"
              fi
            fi
            # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
            # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
            # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
            else
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
                # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
                # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
                # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
                # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
                if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                  -o "$ZIP" \
                  https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi
              done
              got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
              if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
                : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
              elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
                exit 1
              else
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
                rm -f "$ZIP"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # Per-arch keychain: both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted
      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).
      - name: Provision signing via ci-sign (persistent host keychain)
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD
          MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          # gh-1865: the repo copy of ci-sign is authoritative —
          # re-install it to the host PATH on every signing job so
          # ~/bin/ci-sign can never drift from the reviewed source.
          # gh-1954: install(1) does not create parent directories —
          # on a fresh runner $HOME/bin does not exist (run 40822964468,
          # "install: invalid target .../bin/ci-sign: No such file").
          # gh-2030: this install used to live ONLY in the ubuntu-latest
          # `version` job, which never executes ci-sign — the one job that
          # runs it on the signing hosts (this one) never refreshed the
          # copy, so fa-m5 executed a stale pre-gh-2008 script whose
          # set-keychain-settings still raised orphan SecurityAgent dialogs
          # and wedged the x86_64 `security import` for 2h27m (run
          # 41276487426: "User canceled the operation"). Same shape the
          # build-mobile.yml iOS signing step has always used.
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
          install -m 755 scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          if [ -z "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  No signing certificate found — building unsigned (development only)"
            signed=false
            echo "signed=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            signed=true
            echo "✅ Signing certificate found — provisioning via ci-sign..."
            # gh-1865 model v3 (owner decision 2026-10-28): NO per-arch
            # temporary keychains, NO search-list writes, NO default-keychain
            # flips. ~/bin/ci-sign keeps the PERSISTENT ci-signing.keychain-db
            # provisioned (idempotent — concurrent matrix legs re-verify in
            # milliseconds) and pins the identity by SHA-1, so a concurrent
            # leg's same-subject certificate (gh-1865, run 40455401630)
            # cannot shadow resolution. The old per-arch keychain
            # delete+create race was gh-1852; the eviction race was gh-1866;
            # both classes are structurally gone.
            ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos
            CERT_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos)
            CERT_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign name fa-macos)
            echo "identity_sha1=$CERT_SHA1" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "identity_name=$CERT_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "gh-1865: signing identity pinned by SHA-1: $CERT_NAME ($CERT_SHA1)"
            echo "signed=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

          if [ -n "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > profile.provisionprofile
            echo "profile_embedded=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # Make the profile visible to Xcode manual signing. Decoding
            # goes through ci-sign plist — the legacy CMS decoder needs a
            # default keychain, which this model never sets.
            PROFILE_UUID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
            PROFILE_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Name raw -)
            PROFILE_TEAM=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw - 2>/dev/null || true)
            echo "Profile: $PROFILE_NAME / UUID: $PROFILE_UUID / team: $PROFILE_TEAM"
            mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
            cp profile.provisionprofile "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/${PROFILE_UUID}.provisionprofile"
            echo "profile_uuid=$PROFILE_UUID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "profile_team=$PROFILE_TEAM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # gh-1865 fail-fast precheck (owner option B): the profile must
            # embed the provisioned certificate — a mismatch aborts here in
            # seconds instead of surfacing as a dead archive after the full
            # build. Skipped on unsigned runs (no provisioned cert).
            if [ -n "${CERT_SHA1:-}" ]; then
              ~/bin/ci-sign doctor profile.provisionprofile fa-macos
            fi
          else
            echo "⚠️  No provisioning profile found — TestFlight will warn"
            echo "profile_embedded=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi
          # gh-1986: keychain re-unlock WATCHDOG for the whole signing
          # window. The persistent ci-signing.keychain-db auto-locks after
          # ~5 min of inactivity, and `set-keychain-settings -t 0` cannot
          # fix it non-interactively on this host (GUI SecurityAgent
          # prompt — screenshot-confirmed in the Fastfile; ci-sign's
          # bounded attempt is alarm-killed: "Alarm clock: 14" in this
          # step's log). gh-1954's --force host re-provision (run
          # 40857357741, 2026-10-29) re-created the keychain with the
          # locking defaults, and this leg — unlike the iOS gym lane —
          # had no unlock watchdog: run 41008008179 (gh-1986) then hit its
          # FIRST codesign 2h14m after this step's unlock and BOTH matrix
          # archs died with errSecInternalComponent on the same embedded
          # framework (GoogleAppMeasurement), 0.4 s apart. Same fix
          # gh-1954 gave gym: re-unlock every 60 s (unlock-keychain -p
          # never prompts) across build, DMG/PKG packaging, notarize and
          # the no-sandbox build; the always() Cleanup step stops it.
          if [ "$signed" = "true" ]; then
            ~/bin/ci-sign unlock
            nohup bash -c 'while :; do sleep 60; ~/bin/ci-sign unlock >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done' \
              </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
            disown
            echo $! > ci-sign-watchdog.pid
            echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog armed (pid $(cat ci-sign-watchdog.pid), 60s cadence — gh-1986)"
          fi

      - name: Build macOS release (${{ matrix.arch }})
        env:
          # gh-2246: unique per arch + per attempt. A bare run_number is
          # shared by both matrix legs (sibling ASC build/review race) and
          # reused by reruns (altool -19232 "bundle version must be higher
          # than the previously uploaded version"). run_number*10 +
          # run_attempt*2 + archIndex stays monotonic: the next dispatch
          # (+10) always exceeds every attempt/arch combo of the previous
          # run, so a re-upload is always legal.
          # gh-2288: GitHub expression syntax has NO additive '+' — the
          # inline sum made the whole file unparseable (dispatch API 422
          # "Unexpected symbol: '+'", daily cli leg dead, run
          # 44243345944). The raw operands travel as plain env scalars;
          # the run block computes the sum in bash, which has additive
          # arithmetic. Pinned by test/workflow_expression_arithmetic_
          # guard_test.dart (AC2) + build_macos_asc_collision_guard_test.
          RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
          BUILD_VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}

          # THIS job's own keychain right after import) instead of the
          # name-based MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID secret — a concurrent signing
          # leg's same-CN cert in the shared additive search list can no
          # longer shadow the identity at codesign time.
          CERT_SHA1: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.identity_sha1 }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          PROFILE_UUID: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_uuid }}
          PROFILE_TEAM: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_team }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          # gh-2246 BUILD_NUMBER, computed HERE because GitHub expressions
          # have no additive '+' (gh-2288): run_number*10 + run_attempt*2
          # + archIndex stays monotonic — the next dispatch (+10) always
          # exceeds every attempt/arch combo of the previous run.
          if [ "$ARCH" = "arm64" ]; then ARCH_INDEX=1; else ARCH_INDEX=0; fi
          BUILD_NUMBER=$(( RUN_NUMBER * 10 + RUN_ATTEMPT * 2 + ARCH_INDEX ))
          echo "Building for architecture: $ARCH (BUILD_NUMBER=$BUILD_NUMBER)"

            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$CERT_SHA1"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual

              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID"
            elif [ -n "${PROFILE_TEAM:-}" ]; then
              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$PROFILE_TEAM"
            fi

              export FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="$PROFILE_UUID"

            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic

          # --config-only drives the tool's real SPM/pods config pass
          # (the SwiftPM migration + pod install) without compiling; the
          # gate then ASSERTS the adopted SPM lane: SwiftPM state EXPECTED
          # after the config pass (pbxproj marker + ephemeral generated
          # package), app floor 14.0 (pbxproj + Podfile), generated package
          # floor ≥ 14.0 (the tool's silent showBuildSettings bump must
          # have landed — the literal gh-180 killer), no SwiftPM product
          # above the app min, and the vendored inappwebview manifest
          # floored at 14.0 if it ever reappears. A drift fails in seconds
          # with the remediation instead of Xcode's cryptic "requires
          # minimum platform version" error after a 50+-minute resolution
          # pass (gh-1798 measured 3365s on the first Xcode 27 run).
          # gh-1800 follow-up (the residue clean stays): self-hosted
          # workdirs are PERSISTENT — untracked build state (macos/Flutter/
          # ephemeral, Pods, .symlinks) survives actions/checkout, so it is
          # wiped before every build and the config-only pass regenerates a
          # DETERMINISTIC fresh SPM migration + pod install (the pre-#1812
          # runs showed stale residue steering the lane). The gate below
          # then sees exactly the state a fresh 3.47.7 config pass
          # produces.
          flutter clean
          rm -rf macos/Flutter/ephemeral macos/Pods macos/.symlinks
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" flutter build macos --config-only
          bash ../scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh 14.0
          # gh-2075: the package:sqlite3 native-assets hook downloads its
          # prebuilt dylib with ONE un-retried GET during the release
          # build (run 42566734746: the hosted CLI leg got a 504, BOTH
          # self-hosted legs got a proxy error page with HTTP 200 — the
          # hook's sha256 pin caught the wrong bytes ~20 min into each
          # build). Pre-warm the hook's own digest-checked cache now —
          # post-clean, post-config-only (this step's flutter clean wipes
          # .dart_tool; the config pass just recreated it): sha256 pin
          # from the resolved package, atomic tmp+rename writes. A wrong
          # file fails HERE in seconds, never mid-build; a warm cache
          # skips the network entirely. The hook re-validates any cached
          # file against the same pinned digest, so pre-warming is
          # integrity-neutral.
          if [ "$ARCH" = "x86_64" ]; then SQLITE_SEED_ARCH="x64"; else SQLITE_SEED_ARCH="$ARCH"; fi
          # gh-2105: the retired inline 3-attempt prewarm's ~3.5 min
          # budget did not cover the 5+ minute v1.0.697 egress storm —
          # ride the same hardened contract as the composite (gh-2072's
          # sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart: status-gated fetch,
          # exponential backoff, per-request timeouts, attempts: 8 ≈ 10+
          # min of coverage). Copied OUT of the workspace first: a plain
          # dart <path> inside flutter_app builds the package graph's own
          # hooks BEFORE main() — the exact single-attempt download this
          # step exists to bypass (the composite does the same copy).
          # Best-effort (gh-2072 review thread 7): a failed prewarm
          # degrades to the hook's own single-attempt download, never
          # reds the leg by itself. The post-clean position is
          # load-bearing: this step's flutter clean wipes .dart_tool, so
          # the job-level flutter-pub-get prewarm's warmed cache dies
          # here and must be re-warmed.
          cp ../scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm.dart"
          dart "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm.dart" \
            --package-root . \
            --targets "$SQLITE_SEED_ARCH-macos" \
            --attempts 8 \
            || echo "::warning::sqlite3 native-assets prewarm failed — falling back to the hook's own single-attempt download (gh-2072: best-effort, never a red leg by itself)"
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" flutter build macos --release \
            --build-name=$BUILD_VERSION \
            --build-number=$BUILD_NUMBER
          MAIN_BIN=$(find build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app -name "Fa" -type f | head -1)
          echo "=== Binary architecture verification ==="
          echo "Binary path: $MAIN_BIN"
          file "$MAIN_BIN"
          lipo -info "$MAIN_BIN"
          echo "=== End binary verification ==="
          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported
          # the app boots to a white screen on TestFlight — fail here instead.
          echo "=== wasm_run FFI symbol verification ==="
          # dyld_info reads the exports trie, which survives stripping
          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").
          EXPORTS=$(xcrun dyld_info -exports "$MAIN_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"
          for SYM in _wire_compile_wasm _store_dart_post_cobject _init_frb_dart_api_dl; do
            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      - name: Package as DMG

    name: Build Chrome extension
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'

      contents: write

      # train-verification probe (`gh run list` on the tag ref); the
      # probe itself authenticates with RELEASE_PAT (gh prefers

  release-macos:
    name: Create macOS GitHub Release
    needs: [version, build-macos]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # gh-2026: defense-in-depth for the release_tag_mint.sh
      # train-verification probe (`gh run list` on the tag ref); the probe
      # itself authenticates with RELEASE_PAT (gh prefers GH_TOKEN, which
      # every mint-reachable call site exports), so this grant matters
      # only if the probe is ever switched to the job token.
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          path: dmgs
          pattern: Fa-macos-*

        run: ls -laR dmgs/

          python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml
          chmod +x scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh
          scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh dmgs dmgs/latest-mac.yml
          cat dmgs/latest-mac.yml

          # sibling train publishes the derived tag while the serialized
          # self-hosted mac builds are still running (the v1.0.685 daily

          echo "DMGs to upload: $DMGS"
          echo "ZIPs to upload: $ZIPS"

          STABLE_COPIES=()
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")

            # sandboxed build is the default update feed.
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip")
            elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then

          # by construction (cp of the same file). Lowercase `fa-` prefix on

          for dmg in $DMGS; do
            base=$(basename "$dmg")
            if [[ "$base" == fa-macos-nosandbox-arm64-*.dmg ]]; then
              cp "$dmg" "dmgs/fa-nosandbox-macos-arm64.dmg"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-nosandbox-macos-arm64.dmg")
            elif [[ "$base" == fa-macos-nosandbox-x86_64-*.dmg ]]; then
              cp "$dmg" "dmgs/fa-nosandbox-macos-x86_64.dmg"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-nosandbox-macos-x86_64.dmg")
            fi
          done

          # Extract the raw binary from the .app bundle and upload it as the
          # plain asset name (fa-macos-arm64 / fa-macos-x64) so `fa update`
          # and direct downloads work without knowing the version suffix.
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            unzip -qo "$zip" -d /tmp/fa-extract >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            BIN="/tmp/fa-extract/Fa.app/Contents/MacOS/Fa"
            if [ -f "$BIN" ]; then
              if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64")
              elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64")
              fi
              chmod +x "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            rm -rf /tmp/fa-extract
          done
          ASSETS=($DMGS $ZIPS $MANIFEST "${STABLE_COPIES[@]}")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG for your architecture (`arm64` for Apple Silicon, `x86_64` for Intel) and drag Fa.app to Applications. In-app updates use the ZIP + latest-mac.yml feed.\n- **Linux**: Download tar.gz, extract and run the `bundle/fa` binary.\n- **Windows**: Download zip, extract and run the `fa.exe`.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below
          # only ever deletes THIS job's draft, never the mobile leg's
          # mid-upload draft on the same derived tag.
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): the create above uploads
      # assets through a draft — a failed/cancelled run must delete it,
      # never orphan it (the v0.1.190 rot). Ownership-scoped (review of
      # #294): the guard deletes only a draft whose body carries THIS
      # run+job's marker — a sibling leg's draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release).
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || true
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-notes generator (issue #282): useful, mechanical notes for every
# release path — no more "Release v$next" filler bodies.
#
# Usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]
#   version     bare X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z
#   range_start optional git ref for the fallback range (default: the
#               newest tag other than vX.Y.Z itself)
#
# Order of preference:
#   1. the CHANGELOG.md `## <version>` section (curated per-release notes);
#   1b. (gh-1522) the curated `## Unreleased` body — the release flow moves
#      Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE TIME (never in-repo), so
#      a pending Unreleased section IS this release's notes when no
#      versioned section exists yet;
#   2. conventional commits since the previous tag, grouped
#      Features / Fixes / Maintenance, capped at 50 lines with an
#      "…and N more" line (issue #282 E4);
#   3. no commits since the previous tag (re-tag) -> a clean
#      "No changes" body, never an empty page (issue #282 E5/AC5).
set -euo pipefail

version="${1:?usage: release_notes.sh <version> [range_start]}"
version="${version#v}"
range_start="${2:-}"

# ── 1. CHANGELOG.md section for the version ────────────────────────────────
if [ -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
  # gh-1522 rework (PR #1526): more than one `## Unreleased` header is a
  # merge/bot artifact duplicating the curation window — the preference-1b
  # awk below stops at the FIRST header, so the second section's entries
  # would silently never ship. Fail loud instead of publishing notes that
  # dropped content (pinned by the AC5 duplicate-Unreleased test).
  unreleased_count=$(grep -c '^## Unreleased[ \t]*$' CHANGELOG.md || true)
  if [ "$unreleased_count" -gt 1 ]; then
    echo "::error::CHANGELOG.md carries $unreleased_count '## Unreleased' sections — entries past the first silently never ship; keep exactly one (gh-1522 curation convention)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  section=$(awk -v ver="$version" '
    BEGIN { esc = ver; gsub(/\./, "\\.", esc) }
    $0 ~ "^## " esc "[[:space:]]*$" { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
  # gh-1522 preference 1b: a pending curated `## Unreleased` section is
  # this release's notes (the stage-time stamper folds it under the tag's
  # generated section header).
  section=$(awk '
    /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { found = 1; next }
    found && /^## / { exit }
    found { print }
  ' CHANGELOG.md)
  if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "$section" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$section"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# ── 2. conventional-commit fallback ────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -z "$range_start" ]; then
  range_start=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | grep -v -x "v$version" | head -1 || true)
fi

range="HEAD"
[ -n "$range_start" ] && range="$range_start..HEAD"
# The release-bump commit itself is noise in its own release notes.
commits=$(git log "$range" --pretty='%s' --no-merges 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -v '^chore(release):' || true)

if [ -z "$commits" ]; then
  # ── 3. re-tag: nothing changed since the previous release ───────────────
  echo "No changes since ${range_start:-the previous release}."
  exit 0
fi

cap="${RELEASE_NOTES_MAX:-50}"
feats=""; fixes=""; chores=""
shown=0
overflow=0
while IFS= read -r subject; do
  [ -n "$subject" ] || continue
  if [ "$shown" -ge "$cap" ]; then
    overflow=$((overflow + 1))
    continue
  fi
  shown=$((shown + 1))
  case "$subject" in
    feat:*|feat\(*) feats="$feats- $subject
" ;;
    fix:*|fix\(*)  fixes="$fixes- $subject
" ;;
    *)             chores="$chores- $subject
" ;;
  esac
done <<< "$commits"

echo "## What's changed"
echo
[ -n "$feats" ]  && printf '### Features\n%s\n' "$feats"
[ -n "$fixes" ]  && printf '### Fixes\n%s\n' "$fixes"
[ -n "$chores" ] && printf '### Maintenance\n%s\n' "$chores"
[ "$overflow" -gt 0 ] && printf '…and %d more\n' "$overflow"
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-artifact uncompressed size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1).

Emits the per-entry uncompressed size table (the issue's inventory format)
for a shipped artifact and fails the build when any tracked line regresses
beyond the budget (default +5%).

Usage:
  size_manifest.py emit   <artifact> [--min-bytes N]        # TSV to stdout
  size_manifest.py check  <artifact> --baseline FILE
                          [--budget-pct 5] [--init-if-missing]
                          [--manifest-out FILE] [--forbid REGEX]...
                          [--vendored REGEX]... [--strict-vendored]
  size_manifest.py selftest

`<artifact>` is a zip-family file (.zip/.ipa/.aab — uncompressed entry sizes
via zipfile) or a directory (tree of file sizes, for the web deploy root).

Manifest format (TSV; every row is `<bytes>\t<name>`, path-sorted. TOTAL
is an ordinary row — `<total_bytes>\tTOTAL` — and sorts among the paths;
do not rely on its position, the parser keys by name):
  <uncompressed_bytes>\t<path>
  <total_bytes>\tTOTAL

Rev-hash path normalization (#1431): a path segment of 20+ hex chars is
a content/rev-hash directory — the Flutter engine renderer artifacts
(canvaskit/skwasm) move under a new one on every 3.47.x patch drop while
the byte sizes stay identical. Both the artifact scan and the baseline
load collapse such segments to `<rev>` BEFORE diffing, so an engine rev
bump lands as an in-place UPDATE (the usual size-band compare) instead
of N brand-new heavyweight lines. Normalization is idempotent, so
pre-fix baselines carrying the literal rev hash migrate on load — no
baseline rewrite needed. Colliding normalized rows (two rev dirs in one
artifact, e.g. stale files) merge to the heavier one.

Gate semantics (`check`):
  - growth > budget%% on any baseline line or on the first-party TOTAL
    -> FAIL
  - NEW line heavier than 5%% of the baseline first-party TOTAL -> FAIL
    (catches re-adding removed weight, e.g. a dropped interpreter coming
    back — re-growth must be a conscious ack)
  - VENDORED carve-out (#1431): rows under a vendored prefix (default:
    the canvaskit/ engine-renderer subtree; extend with --vendored
    REGEX) are engine payload, not our growth — their breaches print
    ::warning and stay out of the failure count, and they are excluded
    from the TOTAL the budget compares (first-party TOTAL = TOTAL minus
    vendored rows). The engine reving is not the payload growing.
    --strict-vendored turns the carve-out off (everything gates again).
  - removed lines are improvements, reported only
  - --init-if-missing: no baseline file yet -> write it and pass with a
    loud notice (ratchet bootstrap; commit the file to arm the gate)
  - --reseed: overwrite an EXISTING baseline from this artifact and pass
    with a notice — the escape hatch for intentional growth; commit the
    rewritten file to make the new shape the floor
  - --forbid REGEX (repeatable): any manifest row whose path matches
    REGEX fails the check immediately, regardless of the +5% budget or
    the NEW-line share — the deny-list for evicted artifacts (a re-added
    5.6 MB fixture slips under both: NEW share is 5% of TOTAL). Enforced
    on check, --init-if-missing AND --reseed: re-admitting an artifact
    means dropping its --forbid flag, a conscious ack. The deny-list
    floor equals the tracking floor: sub-MIN_BYTES rows never enter the
    manifest.

CI escape hatch for intentional growth: re-run locally with the same
artifact and `--reseed`, commit the rewritten baseline.
"""

import argparse
import re
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

# Per-line tracking floor: smaller files are noise (thousands of them
# jitter by whole percentages); the TOTAL line covers their aggregate.
MIN_BYTES = 64 * 1024
# A brand-new tracked line heavier than this share of the old first-party
# TOTAL is re-growth, not rounding — fail it.
NEW_LINE_SHARE = 0.05
# A path segment of 20+ hex chars is a content/rev-hash directory: the
# Flutter engine renderer artifacts (canvaskit/skwasm wasm) ship under
# `canvaskit/<rev>/` and the rev changes on every 3.47.x patch drop
# (#1431). Collapsed to <rev> on BOTH the artifact scan and the baseline
# load so rev churn diffs as an in-place UPDATE, not N new lines.
REV_SEGMENT_RE = re.compile(r"(^|/)[0-9a-fA-F]{20,}(?=/|$)")
REV_PLACEHOLDER = "<rev>"
# Rows matching a vendored prefix are engine/vendor payload: their
# breaches warn instead of failing (#1431). The canvaskit/ subtree
# carries every engine renderer artifact (canvaskit/skwasm/wimp/
# webparagraph, chromium variant included). First-party paths —
# including our own shipped vendor/interpreters payload — keep the
# full rule.
# The gh-1630 lock-pinned on-device AI engines (vendor/litert,
# vendor/transformers, vendor/webllm — ~82 MB in fa-extension.zip)
# are deliberately NOT carved out (gh-1699 rework decision): they
# ship under version-per-bump paths, so each engine bump enters the
# manifest as a NEW line and hard-fails until the floor is consciously
# reseeded (`check --reseed` + commit) — the documented
# intentional-growth escape hatch. A blanket `(^|/)vendor/` carve-out
# would also de-gate vendor/interpreters (kept first-party above) and
# shrink the NEW_LINE_SHARE base ~3.3x (5% of 117.9 MB -> 5% of
# 35.7 MB), tightening the first-party gate invisibly. If maintainers
# ever want engine churn to warn instead of fail, scope the extra
# --vendored regex to the engine dirs only, e.g.
# r"(^|/)vendor/(litert|transformers|webllm)/", as its own reviewed
# change — not as a side effect of a ratchet reseed.
VENDORED_DEFAULTS = [r"(^|/)canvaskit/"]


def normalize_revpaths(name: str) -> str:
    """Collapse 20+hex path segments (engine rev dirs) to <rev> (#1431)."""
    return REV_SEGMENT_RE.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + REV_PLACEHOLDER, name)


def iter_sizes(artifact: Path):
    """Yield (path, uncompressed_bytes) for every file in the artifact."""
    if artifact.is_file():
        # zip-family: .zip / .ipa / .aab / .apk
        with zipfile.ZipFile(artifact) as zf:
            for info in zf.infolist():
                if info.is_dir():
                    continue
                yield info.filename.replace("\t", " "), info.file_size
        return
    if artifact.is_dir():
        for p in sorted(artifact.rglob("*")):
            if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink():
                yield p.relative_to(artifact).as_posix().replace("\t", " "), p.stat().st_size
        return
    raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: artifact not found: {artifact}")


def build_manifest(artifact: Path, min_bytes: int) -> "dict[str, int]":
    sizes = dict(iter_sizes(artifact))
    manifest = {}
    for p, n in sizes.items():
        if n < min_bytes:
            continue
        key = normalize_revpaths(p)
        # Two rev dirs in one artifact (stale files) collide post-
        # normalization: keep the heavier row on both floor and current.
        if key not in manifest or manifest[key] < n:
            manifest[key] = n
    manifest["TOTAL"] = sum(sizes.values())
    return manifest


def fmt_table(manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> str:
    width = max((len(p) for p in manifest), default=5)
    lines = [f"{manifest[p]:>12}  {p.ljust(width)}" for p in sorted(manifest) if p != "TOTAL"]
    lines.append("-" * (width + 14))
    lines.append(f"{manifest['TOTAL']:>12}  TOTAL")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def load_baseline(path: Path) -> "dict[str, int]":
    baseline = {}
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        size, _, name = line.partition("\t")
        key = normalize_revpaths(name)  # pre-fix literal-rev rows migrate
        if key not in baseline or baseline[key] < int(size):
            baseline[key] = int(size)
    if "TOTAL" not in baseline:
        raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: baseline {path} has no TOTAL line")
    return baseline


def write_baseline(path: Path, manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lines = [f"{manifest[p]}\t{p}" for p in sorted(manifest)]
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


def check(artifact: Path, baseline_path: Path, budget_pct: float,
          init_if_missing: bool = False, reseed: bool = False,
          manifest_out=None, forbid=None, vendored=None,
          strict_vendored=False) -> int:
    manifest = build_manifest(artifact, MIN_BYTES)
    if manifest_out:
        write_baseline(manifest_out, manifest)

    # Deny-list (gh-1331 review): a returning evicted artifact fails the
    # gate in every mode — budget and NEW-line share both miss sub-5%
    # re-adds, so eviction is pinned by pattern, not by the floor.
    forbid_res = [re.compile(p) for p in forbid or []]
    if forbid_res:
        banned = [name for name in sorted(manifest)
                  if name != "TOTAL" and any(r.search(name) for r in forbid_res)]
        if banned:
            for name in banned:
                print(f"::error::size_manifest: FORBIDDEN row in {artifact}: "
                      f"{name} ({manifest[name]} bytes) — matches --forbid; "
                      "the artifact was evicted and must not return")
            return 1

    if not baseline_path.exists():
        if init_if_missing:
            write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
            print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline initialized from this "
                  f"artifact — COMMIT {baseline_path} to arm the gate")
            print(fmt_table(manifest))
            return 0
        print(f"::error::size_manifest: baseline {baseline_path} missing "
              f"(run with --init-if-missing to seed it)")
        return 2

    if reseed:
        write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
        print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline RESEEDED from this "
              f"artifact — {baseline_path} rewritten; COMMIT it to make "
              f"the new shape the floor")
        print(fmt_table(manifest))
        return 0

    baseline = load_baseline(baseline_path)
    base_total = baseline["TOTAL"]
    failures, vendored_failures = [], []
    grew, shrank, new, removed = [], [], [], []

    # Vendored carve-out (#1431): engine/vendor rows breach with a
    # ::warning and never redden the job; the budget's TOTAL compares the
    # first-party aggregate only. --strict-vendored gives the teeth back.
    vendored_res = ([] if strict_vendored
                    else [re.compile(p) for p in VENDORED_DEFAULTS + list(vendored or [])])

    def is_vendored(name: str) -> bool:
        return any(r.search(name) for r in vendored_res)

    def fp_total(manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> int:
        return manifest["TOTAL"] - sum(n for k, n in manifest.items()
                                       if k != "TOTAL" and is_vendored(k))

    for name in sorted(set(baseline) | set(manifest)):
        if name == "TOTAL":
            continue
        old, cur = baseline.get(name), manifest.get(name)
        if old is None and cur is not None:
            new.append((name, cur))
        elif cur is None:
            removed.append((name, old))
        elif cur > old:
            grew.append((name, old, cur))
        elif cur < old:
            shrank.append((name, old, cur))

    for name, old, cur in grew:
        pct = (cur - old) / old * 100 if old else float("inf")
        if pct > budget_pct:
            line = f"  GREW    +{pct:6.1f}%  {name}  {old} -> {cur}"
            (vendored_failures if is_vendored(name) else failures).append(line)
    cur_fp, base_fp = fp_total(manifest), fp_total(baseline)
    fp_total_pct = (cur_fp - base_fp) / base_fp * 100 if base_fp else 0.0
    if fp_total_pct > budget_pct:
        failures.append(f"  TOTAL-1P +{fp_total_pct:6.1f}%  {base_fp} -> {cur_fp} "
                        f"(first-party TOTAL; raw {base_total} -> {manifest['TOTAL']})")
    for name, cur in new:
        if cur > NEW_LINE_SHARE * base_fp:
            line = (f"  NEW     {'':>8}  {name}  {cur} bytes "
                    f"(> {NEW_LINE_SHARE:.0%} of baseline first-party TOTAL)")
            (vendored_failures if is_vendored(name) else failures).append(line)

    print(f"size manifest: {artifact}  (budget: +{budget_pct}% per line, "
          f"baseline: {baseline_path})")
    print(fmt_table(manifest))
    if vendored_failures:
        print(f"::warning::size budget: {len(vendored_failures)} vendored "
              f"line(s) breached in {artifact} — engine/vendor churn, not "
              f"gating (first-party floor untouched):")
        for f in vendored_failures:
            print(f)
    if shrank:
        print(f"improvements: {len(shrank)} line(s) shrank, "
              f"{len(removed)} line(s) removed")
        for name, old, cur in shrank[:10]:
            print(f"  shrank  {name}  {old} -> {cur}")
        for name, old in removed[:10]:
            print(f"  removed {name}  ({old} bytes)")
    if failures:
        print(f"::error::size budget regression in {artifact} "
              f"({len(failures)} line(s) beyond +{budget_pct}%):")
        for f in failures:
            print(f)
        print("intentional growth? re-seed the floor with: python3 "
              "scripts/size_manifest.py check <artifact> --baseline "
              f"{baseline_path} --reseed")
        return 1
    print(f"size budget OK (first-party TOTAL {fp_total_pct:+.1f}% vs baseline)")
    return 0


def selftest() -> int:
    """Synthetic-artifact assertions; exits nonzero on any failure."""
    import tempfile

    ok = True

    def expect(label, actual, wanted):
        nonlocal ok
        status = "ok" if actual == wanted else "FAIL"
        if actual != wanted:
            ok = False
        print(f"  [{status}] {label}: exit {actual} (want {wanted})")

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        td = Path(td)

        def make_zip(path: Path, a_size: int, extra: "dict[str, int] | None" = None):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as zf:
                zf.writestr("bin/a.bin", b"\0" * a_size)
                zf.writestr("bin/b.bin", b"\0" * (10 * 1024))
                for name, size in (extra or {}).items():
                    zf.writestr(name, b"\0" * size)

        base_zip, cur_zip = td / "base.zip", td / "cur.zip"
        make_zip(base_zip, 100 * 1024)
        make_zip(cur_zip, 100 * 1024)
        base = td / "base.tsv"
        r = check(cur_zip, base, 5.0, init_if_missing=True)
        expect("init-if-missing seeds + passes", r, 0)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 104 * 1024)  # +4%: within budget
        expect("within-budget growth passes", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 0)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 106 * 1024)  # +6%: regression
        expect("over-budget growth fails", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 1)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 100 * 1024, {"bin/new.bin": 6 * 1024 * 1024})
        expect("heavy new line fails", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 1)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 80 * 1024)  # still tracked (> 64 KB), 20% smaller
        expect("tracked-line shrink passes", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 0)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 106 * 1024)  # reseed overwrites an EXISTING baseline
        expect("reseed rewrites + passes", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0, reseed=True), 0)
        expect("smaller-than-floor still passes", check(base_zip, base, 5.0), 0)
        bigger = td / "bigger.zip"
        make_zip(bigger, 120 * 1024)  # +13% vs the reseeded floor
        expect("post-reseed regrowth fails", check(bigger, base, 5.0), 1)

        tree = td / "root" / "app"
        (tree / "assets").mkdir(parents=True)
        (tree / "index.html").write_bytes(b"\0" * (200 * 1024))
        (tree / "assets" / "x.bin").write_bytes(b"\0" * (150 * 1024))
        dir_base = td / "dir.tsv"
        expect("dir artifact init", check(tree, dir_base, 5.0, init_if_missing=True), 0)
        (tree / "index.html").write_bytes(b"\0" * (220 * 1024))  # +10%
        expect("dir over-budget fails", check(tree, dir_base, 5.0), 1)

        # Deny-list (gh-1331 review): a re-added evicted row below the
        # NEW-line share (5% of TOTAL) passes the plain gate — only
        # --forbid catches it. Floor: 8 MiB TOTAL -> NEW share ~410 KB;
        # the re-added 100 KB row is tracked (> 64 KB) but sub-share.
        deny_zip, deny_base = td / "deny.zip", td / "deny.tsv"
        make_zip(deny_zip, 100 * 1024, {"bin/big.bin": 8 * 1024 * 1024})
        expect("deny floor seeds", check(deny_zip, deny_base, 5.0, init_if_missing=True), 0)
        make_zip(cur_zip, 100 * 1024,
                 {"bin/big.bin": 8 * 1024 * 1024, "evicted/gone.dat": 100 * 1024})
        expect("re-added sub-NEW-share row passes without --forbid",
               check(cur_zip, deny_base, 5.0), 0)
        expect("re-added row fails with --forbid",
               check(cur_zip, deny_base, 5.0, forbid=["^evicted/"]), 1)
        expect("clean artifact passes with --forbid",
               check(deny_zip, deny_base, 5.0, forbid=["^evicted/"]), 0)
        expect("--forbid blocks reseeding the banned shape",
               check(cur_zip, deny_base, 5.0, reseed=True, forbid=["^evicted/"]), 1)

        # Rev-hash churn (#1431): the engine renderer moves under a new
        # 20+hex rev dir on every 3.47.x patch — pure path substitution,
        # identical bytes. Normalization must diff it as a no-op UPDATE,
        # not N brand-new heavyweight lines; vendored breaches warn; the
        # first-party rule keeps its teeth.
        rev_zip, rev_base = td / "rev.zip", td / "rev.tsv"
        old_rev, new_rev = "a" * 40, "b" * 40

        def make_rev_zip(path: Path, rev: str):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as zf:
                zf.writestr(f"panel/app/canvaskit/{rev}/canvaskit.wasm",
                            b"\0" * (7 * 1024 * 1024))
